- <!-- mem {"id":109,"kind":"fact","confidence":0.95,"provenance":"/home/mrjohn/.config/opencode/scripts/split-serial.sh","topic":"prompt-runner","version":1} --> The canonical split runner is /home/mrjohn/.config/opencode/scripts/split-serial.sh, RUNNER_VERSION=3. It runs one fresh `opencode run` per prompt/*.md file, passes the prompt file's contents rather than a /split command, logs to .scratch/split/<name>.log, and commits each green step as `split: <name>`.
- <!-- mem {"id":110,"kind":"gotcha","confidence":0.9,"provenance":"/home/mrjohn/.config/opencode/scripts/split-serial.sh (detect_check)","topic":"prompt-runner","version":1} --> split-serial.sh detects the gate as `make test && make lint` when those Makefile targets exist, and only falls back to `make check` when neither exists. Defining a lint target therefore prevents `make check` from being the runner's gate.
- <!-- mem {"id":112,"kind":"gotcha","confidence":0.85,"provenance":".scratch/split/runner-from-02.out; .scratch/split/runner-from-29.out; scripts/split-serial.sh git add step","topic":"prompt-runner","version":1} --> When .scratch/ is ignored, split-serial.sh's `git add -A -- . ':(exclude).scratch'` prints `The following paths are ignored by one of your .gitignore files: .scratch` and exits 1, but still stages the other files; the script ignores git add's status and proceeds to commit. Do not treat that message as a failed commit.
